entities.bom:bom.customers: A company that buys our products, such as Kestrel Dynamics or Alpenfluss Technik.
entities.bom:bom.products: A finished product a customer buys. `sku` is the short product code people use in questions (KR-6, SK-9, PU-3); `name` is the long name. A product's parts are found through its assemblies: products.product_id -> assemblies.product_id -> bom_lines.assembly_id -> parts.part_no. `required_certification` and `region_restriction` are the sourcing rules every part of that product must meet.
entities.bom:bom.assemblies: A node in a product's assembly tree (a top-level assembly or a sub-module). Every assembly carries `product_id`, so the product of any assembly is known directly; `parent_assembly_id` is only for the tree.
entities.bom:bom.bom_lines: The bill of materials: one row per part in an assembly with the `quantity` used in one unit of it. To list or cost a product's parts, join bom_lines to assemblies on assembly_id, assemblies to products on product_id, and sum `quantity` where a part appears in more than one assembly.
entities.bom:bom.parts: A part number. `source_type` is custom (made to our drawing), catalog (bought from a catalog) or standard (off-the-shelf). `is_critical` parts need engineering review before they are changed. `shape`, `material_id`, `finish`, `tolerance_mm` and the three dimensions decide whether a catalog item can replace a custom part.
entities.bom:bom.catalog_items: A configurable catalog item that can stand in for a custom part when it has the same `shape`, `material_id` and `finish`, a `min_tolerance_mm` no tighter than the part's `tolerance_mm`, maximum dimensions at least as large as the part's, and a lower price. `distributor_certification` must be AS9120 when the product requires AS9100.
entities.bom:bom.materials: A raw material, with its family and cost per kg.
entities.bom:bom.processes: A manufacturing process, such as 5-axis CNC milling or die casting.
entities.bom:bom.quotes: A supplier quote for a part at a facility. `unit_cost` excludes duties; the landed cost is unit_cost * (1 + tariff_pct / 100). `is_current_source` is true for the one quote each part is bought on today. Parts with a single quote have only one possible source.
entities.bom:bom.suppliers: A supplier company. A supplier can run several facilities.
entities.bom:bom.facilities: A plant or distribution centre that makes or ships parts. `utilization_pct` of 95 or more means it cannot take new work. `region` is North America, Europe or Asia Pacific.
entities.bom:bom.certifications: A quality standard: ISO 9001 (general), AS9100 (aerospace manufacturers, needed for custom aerospace parts), AS9120 (aerospace distributors, needed for catalog and standard parts), NADCAP (special processes).
entities.bom:bom.facility_certifications: Which facility holds which certificate. A certificate is valid only when `expires_on` is on or after today (use CURRENT_DATE, with no parentheses); a facility with an expired certificate does not hold it.
entities.bom:bom.machines: A machine at a facility and the tightest tolerance it can hold. It says what a facility can make; it is not needed to judge a facility's utilization.
entities.bom:bom.approved_vendors: Whether a customer allows a supplier. There is one row per customer and supplier, and `status` is approved, pending or blocked. A supplier is NOT approved when its status is anything other than 'approved'; do not look for suppliers missing from this table.
entities.bom:bom.work_orders: A production run of a part at a facility, with the quantity made and the quantity scrapped (`scrap_quantity`). The scrap rate is scrap_quantity divided by quantity.
entities.bom:bom.nonconformances: A quality defect report on a work order, with its `root_cause`, `severity` and `cost`.
entities.bom:bom.engineering_changes: An engineering change order (ECO) against one part. Open and In review ones are still in progress. The products it affects are those whose assemblies use the part, through bom_lines.
entities.bom:bom.supply_events: A disruption at a facility such as a fire, a certificate lapse, a capacity constraint or a tariff change. `status` is Active or Resolved; `severity` is High, Medium or Low. An active High event means the facility must not be used.
entities.bom:bom.purchase_orders: An order placed for a part at a facility. It was late when `received_date` is after `promised_date`; orders not yet received have no received_date.
entities.bom:bom.inventory: Stock of a part at a facility. A part is below safety stock when `on_hand` is less than `safety_stock`.
entities.bom:bom.dfm_findings: A design-for-manufacturability suggestion for a part, with the percentage it would save. It is safe when `performance_impact` is 'None'; 'Needs engineering validation' ones are excluded from no-risk savings.

metrics:
metrics:
  - name: "landed_cost"
    table: "bom.quotes"
    expression: "unit_cost * (1 + tariff_pct / 100.0)"
    description: "Unit cost plus the import duty on it."
  - name: "scrap_rate"
    table: "bom.work_orders"
    expression: "100.0 * SUM(scrap_quantity) / SUM(quantity)"
    description: "Scrapped units as a percentage of units made."
  - name: "late_delivery"
    table: "bom.purchase_orders"
    expression: "received_date > promised_date"
    description: "A purchase order that arrived after its promised date."
